title: Introduce credential-prefetch adapter and declarative retry profiles; expose pullstream helpers
author: Maya Chen
body: Context: Customers observed elevated tail latency on long-lived streaming connections when credentials are retrieved lazily and when large bursts trigger on-demand reauths. This PR introduces a small, opt-in credential prefetch adapter for the Python SDK, plus a declarative retry profile format and helper that lets applications express retry/backoff semantics in a compact YAML/JSON structure. Motivation: reduce variance during high-concurrency streaming workloads, provide parity with TS/Go SDKs' prefetch semantics, and make retry configuration easier to reason about and share. Summary of changes: - new redwood.auth.prefetch.CredentialPrefetchAdapter: schedules lightweight credential refreshes ahead of their expiry window, supports jittered warmup, and exposes hooks for telemetry. - new redwood.retries.Profile and redwood.retries.from_spec(spec) helper: load retry/backoff presets from a declarative dict (matches format used by TS SDK). - pullstream exports: re-export of PullStream, PullStreamCursor, and PauseToken under redwood.stream for ergonomic imports. - small ergonomic helpers: .with_retry_profile(...) on client builder, and an async context manager warm_prefetch(timeout=...) for quick integration in apps. - tests: unit + integration tests covering warmup edge cases and failure injection. - docs: new docs/quickstarts/prefetch.md and retries/declarative.md included. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for prefetch adapter and retry parser - [x] Integration test with token-failure injection - [x] Compatibility test with TS/Go retry spec - [x] Docs updated (quickstarts + API reference) - [x] Telemetry hooks instrumented (prefix: sdk.auth.prefetch.*) Backwards compatibility: adapter is opt-in; default behavior unchanged. There is one small API addition (client builder helper) that is additive and should not break existing code. If teams use declarative retry specs, they must verify semantics match custom programmatic configs. See SUP-1123 for support notes. Related: aligns with ENG-2149 (server-side credential warmup feature) and follows parity work from TS/Go SDKs.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can we make the prefetch window configurable per-tenant? Prefer not to hardcode 30s — suggested default 15-60s range.
Maya Chen: Added config window_min/window_max with validation; default 20s-45s. Updated tests to cover boundaries.
Lina Morales: The retry spec validator should raise a clear error when unknown keys are present (helpful for user troubleshooting).
Maya Chen: Validator now returns a structured ValidationError with 'unknown_keys' field and a human-readable message. Added tests.
Tomás Ruiz: CI flake on test_prefetch_integration (timing-sensitive). Could we use a deterministic clock in tests?
Maya Chen: Switched tests to use freezegun for deterministic time and added a budgeted sleep macro to avoid flakiness.

issue_discussion_summary: Support case SUP-1123 noted intermittent reauth during heavy burst traffic. This PR reduces probability of reauth storms by warming credentials; server-side feature ENG-2149 complements this to allow short-lived tickets. Support playbook updated with prefetch toggle guidance.
release_notes: Python SDK 1.1.0: Added CredentialPrefetchAdapter (opt-in) to warm credentials for streaming clients; introduced declarative retry profile loader for easier retry config sharing; re-exported PullStream helpers under redwood.stream for ergonomic imports; added telemetry hooks for prefetch events.
manual_steps_for_ops: When enabling prefetch in production, start with conservative window_min=20s and monitor sdk.auth.prefetch.* metrics; if using declarative retry specs, validate them with redwood.retries.validate_spec before rollout.
how_to_use_examples:
1) Builder: client = Client.builder().with_retry_profile('gold').with_prefetch(enabled=True).build()
2) Declarative: spec = {'max_attempts': 5, 'backoff': {'type': 'expo', 'base_ms': 100}, 'jitter': 'full'}
   rprofile = redwood.retries.from_spec(spec)
3) Pullstream import: from redwood.stream import PullStream, PauseToken
notes_from_author: Opted to keep prefetch opt-in to avoid surprising token lifecycles for customers using nonstandard auth providers. The adapter provides hooks so enterprise integrations (HSM/KMS) can plug in metrics and approve refreshes.
